title: Pre- and Post-slaughter Procedures in an Abattoir

lessons.title: Pre-slaughter work in the workplace
lessons.html:
About this work experience

In this module you work in the lairage and at the end of the line under supervision. You will practise the jobs done before slaughter (receiving and preparing cattle) and after slaughter (handling carcasses until dispatch). Your mentor records your progress in your logbook.

Pre-slaughter tasks you will do

  1. Receiving trucks: help line up the truck with the ramp, check the documents and count the cattle as they offload.
  2. Offloading: let cattle walk off calmly. No hitting, shouting or tail twisting.
  3. Checking animals: look for lame, injured, sick or down animals and report them to the supervisor and meat inspector.
  4. Penning: put each lot in its own marked pen, give water and do not overcrowd.
  5. Ante-mortem inspection: help present animals to the meat inspector and follow the inspector's decisions.
  6. Moving to slaughter: move small groups calmly to the race, following the slaughter list.
  7. Lairage hygiene: clean pens and walkways when empty, and keep water troughs clean.

Animal welfare in practice

Your mentor will watch how you handle cattle. Use your position (flight zone and point of balance), flags or paddles, and a quiet voice. Remove objects that scare cattle from the race. Use an electric prodder only if allowed, rarely, and only on the hindquarters. Treating animals with cruelty is an offence under the Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962 and is a dismissible offence at work.

Records

Write down pen numbers, lot numbers, counts and any problems on the lairage sheet. Accurate records make sure every carcass is traced back to its owner.

Safety

Work from catwalks and outside races where possible. Always know your escape route when in a pen. Never stand behind a gate that cattle may push open.

lessons.title: Post-slaughter work in the workplace
lessons.html:
Post-slaughter tasks you will do

  1. Final trim and wash: check carcasses for contamination, trim with a sterilised knife, then wash from the top down.
  2. Inspection support: keep carcass, head and offal numbers matched and follow the meat inspector's instructions. Move detained carcasses to the detention rail.
  3. Weighing and labelling: weigh each side, check the ticket, classification mark and stamp.
  4. Chilling: move carcasses into the chiller, space them so they do not touch, keep doors closed, record temperatures.
  5. By-products and waste: put hides, edible offal, inedible material and condemned material into the correct containers and areas.
  6. Dispatch: check the order and the truck, load hanging carcasses, and complete the dispatch documents.
  7. Cleaning: clean your area at the end of the shift using the correct steps.

How you are assessed

SkillWhat the mentor looks for
HygieneHand washing, knife sterilising, no contamination of carcasses
AccuracyCorrect numbers, labels and records
Following instructionsInspector's decisions carried out exactly
SafetyPPE worn, safe pushing of carcasses, cold-room safety
AttitudeOn time, works with the team, reports problems

Reflecting on your work

At the end of each week, write in your logbook: what you did, what went well, what was difficult, and what you learnt. Ask your mentor for feedback. Talking about mistakes openly is part of learning; hiding them is dangerous in a food plant.

Key points

  • Receive, count and check cattle; report sick or injured animals.
  • Handle cattle calmly and give water and space in the lairage.
  • Keep records so every carcass can be traced.
  • Trim, wash, weigh, label and chill carcasses correctly.
  • Record your work in the logbook and ask for feedback.
